name: Grime’s Graves flint shaft mining
description: Miners dug shafts to access flint and used antler picks to extract nodules at Grime’s Graves.

impact.note: One mining complex using shaft methods already practised elsewhere, giving its region better flint, with no known successors resting on it.

date.label: Approximately 3000–2000 BCE
date.basis: The source reports the date for this scoped event or archaeological context.

events.statement: Historic England dates the flint mine broadly to the Neolithic and Early Bronze Age.

evidence.supports: Historic England dates the flint mine broadly to the Neolithic and Early Bronze Age.
The source attributes this contribution to Grime’s Graves miners.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated case currently researched, not a claim of the capability’s original invention or global priority.

caveats: The range and shaft count cover a long-lived mine complex, not simultaneous activity or the origin of shaft mining.

research.note: Independent review checked Historic England’s site description, broad dating and cumulative minimum shaft count. The count is not annual output or necessarily simultaneous working.

measures.subject: Grime’s Graves mine complex
measures.conditions: At least 433 site-wide shafts reported cumulatively; not contemporary shafts or annual output.

evidence.supports: The record reports at least 433 shafts.
